blocks.text: On the Incident Summary page, you can view aggregate incident counts for a specified date range by using various selectable attributes and filters. Workflow Automation provides several attributes (i.e., summary criteria) that you can use to summarize the number of incidents that have occurred in your organization. This page provides a table that lists the summary criteria attributes, the total incident count for the summary criteria, and the total incident count broken out by either the incident priority or incident severity.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > Workflow Automation > Incident Summary. The Incident Summary page appears, with no information displayed.
See image.
Select a date range for the incidents that you want to summarize on the Incident Summary page.

(Optional) Filter the incidents you want to summarize by selecting one or more filter options. The filter options are the same as those on the Incidents page. To learn more, see Using Incident Filters in Workflow Automation. To reset the filter options, click the Reset icon.
Configure the summary criteria for the incident summary. On the Incident Summary page:

Group by: Select how you want to break out and display the total incident counts that appear in the incident summary. If you want to break out the incident counts by incident priority (e.g., Critical, High, Medium, and Low), select Priority. If you want to break out the incident counts by incident severity (e.g., High, Medium, Low, and Info), select Severity.
Summary Criteria: From the drop-down menu, select the first summary criterion for the incident summary. You can select a maximum of two criteria. Summary criteria are:
Action: The action taken in the incident.
Application Category: The category of the application associated with the incident.
Application Name: The name of the application associated with the incident.
Attachments: Whether the incident has attachments or not. Values are Yes and No.
DLP Type: The type of DLP incident associated with the incident.
Department: The department of the end user who caused the incident.
Destination Type: The Endpoint DLP destination type for the incident.
Dictionary: The DLP dictionary associated with an incident.
Engine: The DLP engine associated with an incident.
File Name: The name of the file associated with the incident.
File Source Location: The path of the file associated with the incident.
File Type: The type or extension of the file associated with the incident.
Home Location: The home location of the end user responsible for the incident.
Originating User Email: The email address of the user responsible for the incident.
Referrer URL: The URL of the previous page a user was on before they performed the action that caused the incident.
Remediation Owner Email: The email address of the person responsible for remediating the incident.
Rule: The DLP rule associated with an incident.
Source DLP Type: The type of DLP policy that the incident violated. Source DLP types are Inline, Email, Endpoint, and SaaS Security.
URL: The URL of the application associated with the incident.
Work Location: The work location of the end user responsible for the incident.
(Optional) Add another summary criterion:
Under the first summary criterion that you added, click Add More.
From the drop-down menu, select the second summary criterion.

To reorder the summary criteria, click the Reorder icon next to a criterion field and drag and drop the criterion in the order that you want. To delete summary criteria, click the Delete icon next to a criterion field.
See image.
Click Submit. The matching incidents appear on the page in a table format.
See image.

Each one of the summary criteria values you configured appears as a column in the table. In addition, the table contains a column for the total incident count for those incidents that match the given criteria, along with columns for the total incident count broken out by incident priority or the severity of the incident. Each row in the table is a specific combination of the summary criteria that triggered incidents along with the total incident count for that combination. This table can display up to 10,000 rows. In the table, you can view the following information:

Summary Criteria: The first one or two columns in the table are titled with the names of the summary criteria you configured for the incident summary (e.g., Dictionary and Engine). The incident values associated with these summary criteria appear in those table columns.
Total: The total number of incidents that match the given summary criteria.
Critical: The total number of incidents with a critical priority that match the given summary criteria. If you selected to group by severity, this column does not appear.
High: The total number of incidents with either a high priority or a high severity that match the given summary criteria. This column depends on the option you selected in the Group by field.
Medium: The total number of incidents with either a medium priority or a medium severity that match the given summary criteria. This column depends on the option you selected in the Group by field.
Low: The total number of incidents with either a low priority or a low severity that match the given summary criteria. This column depends on the option you selected in the Group by field.
Info: The total number of incidents with an info severity that match the given summary criteria. If you selected to group by priority, this column does not appear.

When you click any of these links, a new tab opens, displaying the Selected Criteria page. The tab is labeled with the criteria associated with the link. This page displays the criteria associated with the link in the Selected Criteria section of the page, and lists the actual incidents with the relevant filters applied for that combination of criteria. This page is similar to the Incidents page except that no action can be taken on an incident. To learn more, see Managing Incidents.
See image.

blocks.text: The Incident Summary page allows you to perform certain actions to manage the incident summaries.

blocks.item: Apply Time Range Filter

You can filter the incidents summarized on the Incident Summary page by the date and time of occurrence. By default, this page summarizes information about the incidents that occurred in the current calendar week (Sunday through Saturday). Time ranges are:
Hours
Current Hour
Last Hour
Last 2 Hours
Last 6 Hours
Last 12 Hours
Days
Current Day
Last Day
Weeks
Current Week
Last Week
Months
Current Month
Last Month
Custom Date Range
To view the incidents that occurred in a specific date range, you can use the Custom Date Range option and specify the start and end dates and times. To specify a custom date range:
Select the Custom Date Range option. A calendar appears with the current date selected. To the right of the calendar, three columns appear, displaying the hours, minutes, and seconds for a day.
See image.

Select the start date on the calendar, and then in the columns to the right, select the start time (i.e., hour, minute, and second). As you select the date and time, they appear in the Start date field under the calendar.
See image.
Click OK. The date and time you selected appear in the Start date field, and the End date field is selected.
Select the end date in the calendar, and then in the columns to the right, select the end time (i.e., hour, minute, and second).
See image.
Click OK.
The Custom Date Range option only supports incidents that are up to 6 months old, and you can only search for a maximum of a three-month window.
See image.
Export an Incident Summary
You can export the information that appears in the Incident Summary table to a CSV file. To export the incident summary:
On the Incident Summary page, configure the summary criteria.
Click Submit. The Incident Summary table appears.
Click the Export icon at the top right of the table. A CSV file is created and downloaded to your local system. The CSV file lists the information that is in the incident summary table.
See image.
Manage Summary Criteria
On the Incident Summary page, you can manage the summary criteria for the incident summaries that appear on the page. You can do the following:
Save Summary Criteria
To save summary criteria:
On the Incident Summary page, configure the summary criteria.
Click Save. The Save Criteria dialog window appears.
In the Save Criteria dialog window, enter a name for the combination of summary criteria in the Name field.
(Optional) If you want the summary criteria combination to appear by default on the Incident Summary page, select Set as default.
See image.

Click Save As. The set of summary criteria is saved and appears in the Saved Criteria field. After you save the summary criteria combination, you can reuse it by selecting it from the Saved Criteria drop-down menu at the top of the page. If you set it as the default criteria, the system automatically selects it in the Saved Criteria drop-down menu when you access the page at a later date.
Apply Saved Summary Criteria

To apply saved summary criteria, select the saved summary criteria name from the Saved Criteria drop-down menu at the top of the page. The Incident Summary page appears, displaying the incident summary table and displaying the fields for the saved summary criteria on the left side of the page.
See image.
Update Saved Summary Criteria
To update saved summary criteria:

On the Incident Summary page, select the saved summary criteria from the Saved Criteria drop-down menu. The Incident Summary page appears, displaying the incident summary table and displaying the fields for the saved summary criteria on the left side of the page.
See image.
Modify the summary criteria. You can:
Change the Group by option.
Delete existing summary criteria.
Add new summary criteria. You can only add another criterion if there is already one criterion saved.
Rearrange the order of the summary criteria.
See image.
Click Update.
Delete Saved Summary Criteria
To delete saved summary criteria:

On the Incident Summary page, from the Saved Criteria drop-down menu, click the Delete icon next to the saved summary criteria that you want to delete. A message appears asking whether you are sure that you want to delete the saved summary criteria.
See image.
Click Yes. The saved summary criteria are deleted.
Modify Items Per Page
To modify the number of items displayed per page, click the Items per page drop-down menu and select the number of items. Options are 10, 20, 25, 50, and 100. The default display is 10.
See image.
